description: The bar chart illustrates the performance comparison of two multilingual BERT models — mBERT and XLM-R — across various language families, based on the number of tasks where each model performed “better” or “same” relative to the other, as measured by task count. The horizontal axis lists nine language families: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis represents “task count,” ranging from 0 to 40, with tick marks at intervals of 10. Each language family has three grouped bars: light blue for “mBERT better,” dark blue for “XLM-R better,” and light green for “same.” For example, in IE-Slavic, XLM-R significantly outperforms mBERT with a task count of ~39, while mBERT is better in only ~12 tasks, and ~28 tasks are tied. In contrast, for IE-Germanic, XLM-R leads with ~18 tasks, mBERT with ~4, and ~22 are tied. In IE-Romance, XLM-R leads with ~13, mBERT with ~4, and ~30 are tied. In IE-Baltic, XLM-R leads with ~10, mBERT with ~0, and ~7 are tied. For IE-Indic, XLM-R leads with ~5, mBERT with ~1, and ~4 are tied. For IE-other, XLM-R leads with ~6, mBERT with ~1, and ~8 are tied. For Isolate, XLM-R leads with ~5, mBERT with ~1, and ~1 is tied. For Semitic, XLM-R leads with ~7, mBERT with ~0, and ~1 is tied. For Uralic, XLM-R leads with ~14, mBERT with ~1, and ~5 are tied. The chart visually emphasizes that XLM-R generally outperforms mBERT across most language families, particularly in IE-Slavic, while “same” performance is most frequent in IE-Romance and IE-Germanic.
